cards.text: This prayer comes with a label on top: it's a prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the LORD. No name, just a worn-out man talking straight to God. He opens with “Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry for help come before You.”

cards.question: The worn-out man asks the LORD to take His time and answer him whenever He's ready.

cards.text: He asks God not to hide His face from him in his day of distress, and to “answer me quickly when I call.” Friend, this man is NOT leaving a polite voicemail and waiting by the phone.

cards.question: Then the man tells God why he's in such a hurry. He says his days vanish like smoke. What's he saying about his life?

cards.text: His bones burn like glowing embers. His heart is afflicted, withered like grass.

cards.question: The afflicted man says he even forgets to ___ his bread.

cards.text: Through his loud groaning, his skin hangs on his bones. I live in a BAKERY with cookie dough on every spoon, so friend, I have NEVER forgotten to eat, not ONCE.

cards.question: The man says he is like a desert owl, like an owl among the ruins, and like a lone bird on a housetop. What do these pictures say about how he feels?

answers.text: He feels ready to fly home

cards.text: He lies awake, too. Friend, I did years of lying awake in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, the view is MOSTLY dust.

cards.question: Besides feeling all alone, the man says his enemies taunt him all day long.

cards.text: They ridicule him and curse him too. He says he has eaten ashes like bread and mixed his drink with tears, and friend, that is the saddest menu I have EVER heard.

cards.question: The man has been eating ashes like bread and mixing his drink with tears. What does he say all this sorrow comes from?

cards.text: He tells the LORD, “You have picked me up and cast me aside.” I think that line hurts the most.

cards.question: Then the man says his days are like lengthening shadows, and he withers away like grass. What time of day does that shadow picture bring to mind?

cards.text: Then the whole prayer turns on one little word: But. Friend, the man stops looking down at himself and looks up at the LORD.

cards.question: The man's own days are fading. What does he say about the LORD?

answers.text: He is far off and silent
He has grown tired of Zion

cards.text: His renown endures to all generations, too. Then the man turns to Zion, the city of Jerusalem, and tells the LORD He will rise up and have compassion on her.

cards.question: The man says Zion will have to wait a long time for the LORD's favor, because her appointed time hasn't come yet.

cards.text: The man says God's servants delight in Zion's stones and take pity on her dust.

cards.question: When the LORD shows Zion favor, the man says the nations will fear the name of the LORD.
God's servants take pity on Zion's dust. Then the man says the LORD will ___ Zion.
Right after saying the LORD has appeared in His glory, the man says the LORD will despise the prayer of the destitute.

cards.text: The LORD will turn toward the prayer of the destitute, and “He will not despise their prayer.”

cards.question: The man says, “Let this be written for the generation to come…” Why does he want it written down?

answers.text: So future people can praise the LORD
So future people can remember him
So future people can avoid his trouble

cards.text: I bet he never pictured a cookie stamper with a giant French mustache reading it, friend. Then he tells how the LORD looked down from the heights of His sanctuary, from heaven to earth.

cards.question: The LORD gazed out from heaven to earth. What did He look down to hear?
The LORD heard a prisoner's groaning. He also looked down to ___ those condemned to death.

cards.text: All so that they may proclaim the name of the LORD in Zion and praise Him in Jerusalem, when peoples and kingdoms assemble to serve the LORD. Friend, that's a LOT of people in one place, and not one of them is there for the cookies.
Whew, friend. The man comes right back down to his own trouble, and he doesn't hold back: “He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.”

cards.question: His strength is broken and his days are cut short. What does the man ask God?

answers.text: Not to take him in the middle of his days
To take him home right away
To send his enemies far away

cards.text: He tells God, “Your years go on through all generations.” In the beginning God laid the foundations of the earth and made the heavens with His hands, and friend, I get proud of ONE good batch.

cards.question: The earth and the heavens are the work of God's hands. What does the man say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will perish and wear out

cards.text: They will wear out like a garment, and like clothing God will change them. But the man tells God, “You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”

cards.question: The man ends his prayer by saying the children of God's servants will have to live in fear.
